sections_target.text: Chemical preservation of boilers is used to protect them from corrosion during the period the boiler is out of service, using the corrosion inhibitor at concentrations much higher than those used during operation, to preserve the magnetite layer covering the internal surfaces of the boiler (water sides) and to eliminate any leakage of oxygen, which causes corrosion. Since wet preservation is suitable at Mahmoudia Station, wet preservation is used.

This document was prepared by Chemist Fayez Fathy Habib and Engineer Mohamed Mohie El-Din Rishou, reviewed by Engineer Hala Hosny Hassan, Manager of the Chemistry Department, and approved by Engineer Mohamed Abdel Azim Saleh, Head of Mahmoudia Generation Station Sector.

This document was reviewed by Chemist Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel, Chemistry Inspector in the Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, approved by Engineer Samir Abdel Galil Ahmed, General Manager and MPIS Documents Coordinator, and certified by Engineer Mohamed Nageeb Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.

rows: Since the inhibitor is used in large quantities, it is essential to take full safety precautions for those handling it, such as:
Wearing the personnel uniform and a gas mask.
Placing Safety Tags on valves and instruments when needed.
Using a Loading Pump to transfer the chemicals to the concentrated tanks, as they will be used directly for injection.
Injection pumps - daily treatment chemicals tank.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as gloves and safety shoes, etc.
Shutdown of the boiler in combined-cycle mode.
As soon as the diverter valve is closed, the main steam valve (S.H.S) is closed.
Shut down the (heat recovery steam generator) using the Stop Sequence.
Close the continuous and emergency blowdown valves on the HP drum (a high level in the drum is not important in this case).
When the feed tank temperature drops below 95 °C.
Hydrazine is injected through the main pump and the standby pumps, into the suction of the L.P pumps, then to the LP evaporator, then to the feed tank, with continuous recirculation.

The water and the hydrazine it contains are transferred to the LP and HP sections using the feed pumps, after draining the "HP drum"; the HP pump is run for recirculation, then the HP drum level is brought to "700 mm", opening the vents and bringing the water through them, then closing them.

When hydrazine injection is complete, the pressure is brought to 2-3 bar using the condensate pumps, keeping the (F.W. & H.P & L.P) pumps in recirculation mode for 15 minutes, then the (H.P & L.P) pumps are run for one hour daily.
The feed pump is run once a week for 15 minutes.
Before shutdown, the recirculation pumps (F.W.P & H.P & L.P) are run; a sample is taken and the hydrazine percentage and pH are followed up.
The boiler is topped up using the condensate pump at a Flow rate = 13 t/h, with injection of additional chemicals if the specifications, pressure or level drop.

sections_target.text: Steps for returning the boiler to service after preservation periods

rows: All valves must be inspected and maintenance tags removed after putting the valves in their normal position.

Use the low-pressure pumps (LP) and the high-pressure pumps (FWP and HP) in recirculation for one hour, to convert corrosion products, if any, into suspended products that are easy to remove on blowdown.
Blow down the feed tank and the high-pressure drum until the (HH) alarm disappears.
Open the "Stack damper".
Raise the "HP drum" pressure to 5 bar by partially opening the "diverter valve".
Close the "Diverter valve", stop the "FP & HP & LP" pumps, and drain the boiler through it.
Open the manual valve "Screw Down - Non Return valve" and open the blowdown valves on the main steam line.
Refill the boiler, the feed tank and the high-pressure circuits, with a small injection of hydrazine.
The boiler is returned to service with the continuous blowdown valve open, and the emergency valve is also used to reach the required specifications.
Hydrazine Used
Preservation Period
66 litres, 24% (N2H4), in the suction of the LP pumps.
From one month to 6 months

These quantities are calculated on 55 m3 of water, the total volume of the boiler. The hydrazine percentage must not fall below 50 ppm during the long preservation period. The pH value in the high-pressure circuit and the high-pressure drum is raised to 11 using sodium hydroxide and trisodium phosphate. The rate of decline of the hydrazine percentage is followed up over time.

Introduction
Chemical preservation of boilers is used to protect them from corrosion during the period the boiler is out of service, using the corrosion inhibitor at concentrations much higher than those used during operation, to preserve the magnetite layer covering the internal surfaces of the boiler (water sides) and to eliminate any leakage of oxygen, which causes corrosion. Since wet preservation is suitable at Mahmoudia Station, wet preservation is used.
This document was prepared by Chemist Fayez Fathy Habib and Engineer Mohamed Mohie El-Din Rishou, reviewed by Engineer Hala Hosny Hassan, Manager of the Chemistry Department, and approved by Engineer Mohamed Abdel Azim Saleh, Head of Mahmoudia Generation Station Sector.
This document was reviewed by Chemist Mohamed Mosbah Mokpel, Chemistry Inspector in the Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, approved by Engineer Samir Abdel Galil Ahmed, General Manager and MPIS Documents Coordinator, and certified by Engineer Mohamed Nageeb Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector of the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.
Safety Precautions
Since the inhibitor is used in large quantities, it is essential to take full safety precautions for those handling it, such as:
Wearing the personnel uniform and a gas mask. | 1
Placing Safety Tags on valves and instruments when needed. | 2
Using a Loading Pump to transfer the chemicals to the concentrated tanks, as they will be used directly for injection. | 3
Tools and Equipment Used
Injection pumps - daily treatment chemicals tank. | 
Occupational safety and health equipment such as gloves and safety shoes, etc. |

When the feed tank temperature drops below 95 °C. | 5
Hydrazine is injected through the main pump and the standby pumps, into the suction of the L.P pumps, then to the LP evaporator, then to the feed tank, with continuous recirculation. | 6

When hydrazine injection is complete, the pressure is brought to 2-3 bar using the condensate pumps, keeping the (F.W. & H.P & L.P) pumps in recirculation mode for 15 minutes, then the (H.P & L.P) pumps are run for one hour daily. | 8
The feed pump is run once a week for 15 minutes. | 9

All valves must be inspected and maintenance tags removed after putting the valves in their normal position.

Blow down the feed tank and the high-pressure drum until the (HH) alarm disappears. | 2 | 
Open the "Stack damper". | 3 | 
Raise the "HP drum" pressure to 5 bar by partially opening the "diverter valve". | 4 |

Open the manual valve "Screw Down - Non Return valve" and open the blowdown valves on the main steam line. | 6 | 
Refill the boiler, the feed tank and the high-pressure circuits, with a small injection of hydrazine. | 7 | 
The boiler is returned to service with the continuous blowdown valve open, and the emergency valve is also used to reach the required specifications. | 8 |
